obligation: Report actual or threatened cyber incident (Coast Guard, FBI, CISA)
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering a terminal, including its data, networks and systems (for example a ransom note on ETOP, encryption of gate servers, or suspicious activity reaching OT)
deadline: Immediately
notify: The Captain of the Port of every affected COTP zone (Sector command center numbers in each FSP and incident binder), the FBI field office and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 8 waterfront facilities in 5 COTP zones. CySO reports; a Terminal OT Security Lead (alternate CySO) if the CySO cannot be reached. Does not wait for forensics, counsel or the materiality decision
clock_starts: When the evidence is first seen by any responder (record the time)

obligation: Reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center (fallback)
trigger: A reportable cyber incident that has not been reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if no 6.16-1 report was made. A 6.16-1 report to the Coast Guard satisfies this duty

trigger: Activities that may result in a transportation security incident (for example attackers targeting PACS, CCTV or crane controllers)
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each FSO decides under the FSP
owner: Facility Security Officer of each affected terminal

citation: 33 CFR 101.305(b); breach of security defined in 101.105
trigger: FSP security measures circumvented, eluded or violated without a TSI (for example TWIC access control or CCTV disabled by the attack)
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if FSP measures are affected - FSO decides
owner: Facility Security Officer of each affected terminal

trigger: A security incident causing significant loss of life, environmental damage, transportation system disruption or economic disruption in a particular area (for example a multi-day closure of several terminals at a port)
deadline: Without delay, then follow the FSP procedures
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the outage reaches TSI level - FSO and the COO decide with the COTP
clock_starts: When the FSO and COO determine the threshold may be met

trigger: Any reportable cyber incident or cyber threat
deadline: Create during the incident; keep at least 2 years, protected from unauthorized deletion or amendment
notify: Incident record in SOC case management and the FSO records system; CySO reports the incident to the owner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - at every affected facility

citation: SL-2 client agreements (contract); supports the clients' own duties under 6.16-1 and the without-delay vendor notice expected under 101.650(f)(2)
trigger: Incident affecting or possibly affecting a client's ETOP environment
deadline: Without delay, target 1 hour (POL-03 4.8). Current agreements say 24 hours until amended (POAM-011)
notify: Each affected client's CySO and FSO by phone, then written notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 4 clients (C-01 to C-04), each an MTSA facility operator with its own reporting duties

obligation: Vendor notice of vulnerabilities or reportable cyber incidents (inbound)
trigger: A vendor or service provider (TOS vendor, OEM, cloud, customs data exchange) has a reportable cyber incident or a vulnerability affecting company IT or OT
deadline: Without delay (contract clause; missing at 31% of tier-1 vendors and all port partners, POAM-022)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Any cybersecurity incident that may be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: Discovery of the incident; the committee convenes within 48 hours of declaration (POL-03 4.5)

trigger: Incident determined to be material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: Date and time of the materiality determination

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General sets
notify: Department of Justice through outside counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - possible for port incidents with national security aspects

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - incident lessons feed the next disclosure

trigger: Severity-1 incident under materiality review
deadline: At once
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information (for example driver names with driver license numbers, or employee records)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay, or a fixed number of days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - drivers, employees and longshore workers reside in many states
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above each state's threshold
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where thresholds are met

trigger: Notices above each state's count
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where counts are met

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days only on written good cause to the Department)
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida terminals, headquarters and drivers
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
clock_starts: When the individual notices are sent

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
deadline: For the period the agency specifies in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the FBI or another agency asks

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the determination is made

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound, worked example)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example the payroll provider or the SL-1 messaging service) has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after the agent determines the breach
notify: The company (General Counsel); the company then gives the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (T-08 inherited contracts under review, POAM-022)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated rail, transit or pipeline operator
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification (SD Sec. II.C; verified for SD 1580-21-01E and SD Pipeline-2021-01G 2026-10-05); supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a TSA-designated operator (N48-49-R02, R03); on-dock rail partners report under their own directives

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or services found in use under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

trigger: Covered article found under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Incident affecting vessel work, berth windows or EDI
deadline: Per each agreement; operationally as soon as vessel work or EDI is affected
notify: Carrier operations centers and vessel agents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational

obligation: Port authorities and port community systems
citation: Concession and lease agreements; data exchange terms (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting terminal operations or data exchanged with the port
deadline: Per each agreement; operationally at once when gates or EDI are suspended
notify: Port authority operations and security; port community system operators
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 6 ports

obligation: Customs data exchange service and CTPAT contact
trigger: Incident affecting hold and release data or the integrity of release decisions
deadline: At once operationally (suspend automated releases); program notice per CTPAT guidance as advised by counsel
notify: Customs data exchange provider; CTPAT supply chain security specialist
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - partner since 2019

obligation: SL-1 customers (trucking companies, cargo owners, brokers)
trigger: Incident affecting SL-1 availability or data
deadline: Per SL-1 terms; status page within 1 hour
notify: Portal banner, status page and API customer email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
